drafts.subject: chr:entity:battle-of-actium
drafts.quotation: Actium was one of the decisive battles of the world
drafts.rationale: Hale calls Actium one of the decisive battles of the world, so the battle is an instance of the concept of a decisive battle in his reading.
drafts.relevance: It records the author's evaluation of the battle as decisive.

notes.note: Hale reads Actium as the event that fixed the Roman Empire's destiny for centuries and enabled Octavian to found the imperial system as Augustus while keeping Republican forms.
notes.quotation: the event that fixed the destinies of the Roman Empire for centuries to come, made Octavian its dictator

notes.note: Hale gives the background to the war: Antony's Orientalization and his plan to move the Empire's centre to Alexandria and found a dynasty with Cleopatra, which strengthened Western loyalty to Octavian.
notes.quotation: Antony spoke openly of making Alexandria and not Rome the centre of the Empire, and of founding with the Egyptian Queen a new dynasty that would rule East and West from the Nile.
